nodes.en: Holistic study of human cultures, both past and present, examining material culture, social organization, language, and biological variation across societies.
nodes.cs: Holistické studium lidských kultur, minulých i současných, zkoumající hmotnou kulturu, sociální organizaci a jazykové rozdíly.
nodes.brief:
Anthropology is the holistic study of human cultures, past and present, encompassing material culture, social organization, language, and biological variation across societies. It distinguishes itself from [[04.02]] Sociology by its comparative, often long-durée and cross-cultural approach, and from [[04.01]] Psychology by treating the individual as inseparable from the cultural system that gives their behavior meaning.

Its subfields split along method and evidence: living communities are studied through ethnographic fieldwork, languages through linguistic analysis, human biological variation through physical anthropology, and vanished societies through [[04.10]] Archaeology, which reconstructs past cultures from excavated material remains rather than living informants. The discipline's attention to settlement patterns and cultural distribution also connects it to [[04.08]] Geography, which supplies the spatial framework for interpreting where and why cultures took the forms they did.

Anthropology's four-field tradition, cultural, linguistic, biological, and archaeological, remains a distinguishing feature of the discipline in North America, though the branches operate largely independently elsewhere. The [American Anthropological Association](https://www.americananthro.org/AdvanceYourCareer/Content.aspx?ItemNumber=1971) sets out the field's scope and ethical standards, and the [Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy entry on relativism](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/relativism/) addresses the methodological debate at the discipline's core.

nodes.name: Social and Cultural Anthropology
nodes.en: The comparative study of human societies and their meanings, built on long-term participant observation rather than survey or experiment. Its characteristic claim is that practices which look irrational from outside are coherent from within.
nodes.cs: Srovnávací studium lidských společností a jejich významů, založené na dlouhodobém zúčastněném pozorování, nikoli na dotazníku či experimentu. Jeho charakteristickým tvrzením je, že praktiky zvenčí nesmyslné jsou zevnitř soudržné.

nodes.name: Biological Anthropology
nodes.en: Humans as a biological species: evolution, variation, primatology and the relationship between biology and behaviour.
nodes.cs: Člověk jako biologický druh: evoluce, variabilita, primatologie a vztah mezi biologií a chováním.

nodes.name: Linguistic Anthropology
nodes.en: Language as cultural practice — how speech constructs identity, relationship and social order, rather than merely describing them.
nodes.cs: Jazyk jako kulturní praxe — jak řeč vytváří identitu, vztah a společenský řád, spíše než aby je jen popisovala.

nodes.name: Ethnography and Fieldwork
nodes.en: The method: entering a setting, participating, recording, and the reflexive problem of the observer as part of what is observed.
nodes.cs: Metoda: vstup do prostředí, účast, záznam a reflexivní problém pozorovatele jako součásti pozorovaného.

nodes.name: Kinship, Exchange and Ritual
nodes.en: The classical subjects — descent and alliance, gift and reciprocity, rite and symbol — through which the discipline built its theory.
nodes.cs: Klasická témata — původ a spříznění, dar a reciprocita, obřad a symbol — na nichž obor vybudoval svou teorii.

nodes.name: Applied and Medical Anthropology
nodes.en: The discipline used practically: in health, development and organisations, and the ethical questions that use raises.
nodes.cs: Obor v praktickém užití: ve zdravotnictví, rozvoji a organizacích, a etické otázky, které takové užití vyvolává.
